title: Normalized scalar-completion associator data
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an arbitrary scheme $W$ on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every finite field extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ be the published completed coefficient ring sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], let $D_E$ be the unbounded derived category of its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and use quotient-tower derived completeness [def-weil-derived-complete]. For every $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra map $\iota:E\to F$, write $T_\iota:D_E\to D_F$ for ordinary derived tensor with $R_F$, $I_\iota:D_E\to D_F$ for the published strict-tower scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $\chi_\iota:T_\iota\to I_\iota$ for its actual quotient-cocone completion comparison [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use the published flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], ordinary termwise scalar functors and their canonical derived counits, and restriction to the quotient coefficient rings [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The resolution-independent interpretation of $I$ is the one of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]; the ordinary derived tensor is that of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Composition in the formulas below is right to left.

Define the normalized scalar-completion associator datum on $W$ to be the following structure, simultaneously for all these fields and coefficient maps (including identity maps):
(1) A proof that $I_\iota$ preserves derived-complete inputs.
(2) Natural ordinary associators $a^T_{\kappa,\iota}:T_\kappa T_\iota\simeq T_{\kappa\iota}$ for every $E\xrightarrow\iota F\xrightarrow\kappa L$. On every flat-term K-flat representative $P$, there must be an isomorphism $a_P$ between the corresponding termwise tensor complexes, carrying $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $c\,\widehat\kappa(b)\otimes x$ in every degree and on every pro-etale object. Its localization is required to compute the chosen derived associator: $Q(a_P)\epsilon_{\kappa,T_\iota P}T_\kappa(\epsilon_{\iota,P})=\epsilon_{\kappa\iota,P}a^T_{\kappa,\iota,QP}$, where $\epsilon$ denotes the published derived scalar counit.
(3) Ordinary multiplication unitors $u^T_E:T_{1_E}\simeq1_{D_E}$ whose components on every such $P$ are the derived counit followed by the localization of the published ordinary scalar identity multiplication.
(4) Natural completed associators $a^I_{\kappa,\iota}:I_\kappa I_\iota\simeq I_{\kappa\iota}$ on the full subcategory of derived-complete $K\in D_E$, normalized by
$$a^I_{\kappa,\iota,K}\,I_\kappa(\chi_{\iota,K})\,\chi_{\kappa,T_\iota K}=\chi_{\kappa\iota,K}\,a^T_{\kappa,\iota,K}.$$
Every other natural isomorphism on the same full subcategory satisfying this equation must equal $a^I_{\kappa,\iota}$; this is the independence/uniqueness field, not an unspecified choice of maps.
(5) Completed unitors $u^I_E:I_{1_E}\simeq1$ on derived-complete inputs, normalized by $u^I_{E,K}\chi_{1_E,K}=u^T_{E,K}$.
(6) For every fourth field and map $\nu:L\to M$ and every complete $K\in D_E$, the pentagon equation
$$a^I_{\nu,\kappa\iota,K}\,I_\nu(a^I_{\kappa,\iota,K})=a^I_{\nu\kappa,\iota,K}\,a^I_{\nu,\kappa,I_\iota K}.$$
The intermediate input $I_\iota K$ uses the completeness proof from (1). The two unit equations are $a^I_{\iota,1_E,K}=I_\iota(u^I_{E,K})$ and $a^I_{1_F,\iota,K}=u^I_{F,I_\iota K}$.

This defines the data type; it does not assert that it is inhabited. There is no boundedness, constructibility, dimension, Noetherian or nonemptiness hypothesis on $W$, and the coefficient-field and scheme universes are independent.
